In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for our data set, the temporal structure of MT spike trains does not contain any significant amount of information beyond that already contained in the mean firing rate.
the majority of the neurons in the visual system are not oscillatory.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found no statistically significant evidence for the existence of an explicitly oscillating neuronal mechanism that would contribute to the encoding of information in the temporal structure.
the power spectrum of bursting cells in MT is compatible with a model in which the cells fire Poisson bursts.
we have shown that a peak in the spectrum of a spike train does not necessarily indicate that the underlying process is oscillatory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the power spectrum of MT cells is flat in the low frequency range, but it shows a peak at 30-50 Hz.
the temporal fine structure in the spike trains of MT neurons can be accounted for by a simple model of Poisson bursts.
the power spectra of many MT neurons are compatible with the assumption that they fire Poisson-distribution spikes.
